questions.q: What is a table calculation, fundamentally?
options: A calculation applied after Tableau has already aggregated data into the rows and columns visible in the view
A calculated field evaluated against the raw, unaggregated data source
A type of filter that hides rows from the view
A setting that changes a field's data type
questions.explain: Table calculations recompute values from what's already aggregated and showing in the view — totals, ranks, running sums — rather than from the original detail rows.

questions.q: What's the closest SQL concept to a Tableau table calculation?
options: A window function, like SUM(Sales) OVER (ORDER BY Month ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING)
A plain GROUP BY aggregate with no OVER clause
A WHERE clause filter
A CREATE TABLE statement
questions.explain: A window function computes a value from already-aggregated rows in a specified order/partition — exactly what a Tableau table calculation does to the values already in the view.

questions.q: How can you tell, just by looking at a pill in Tableau, that a field has a table calculation applied?
options: A small triangle icon appears on the pill
The pill turns from blue to green
The pill's text becomes bold
There is no visual indicator — you must check the underlying formula every time
questions.explain: Any field carrying a table calculation gets a small triangle badge on its pill, which is the visual tell that its values are being recomputed after aggregation.

questions.q: What do table calculation functions like RUNNING_SUM and WINDOW_AVG typically wrap?
options: An already-aggregated value, such as SUM([Sales]), not a raw unaggregated column
A raw column name with no aggregation applied
A string literal
A boolean filter expression
questions.explain: Table calc functions operate on values already aggregated into the view — they wrap an aggregation like SUM([Sales]), and Tableau typically flags it as invalid if you try to wrap a bare, unaggregated field.

questions.q: How is a table calculation different from the calculated fields covered earlier in this course?
options: A calculated field is evaluated against the underlying data source before aggregation; a table calculation is applied after the data is already aggregated into the view
They are the same thing with two different names
Calculated fields can only produce text, while table calculations can only produce numbers
Table calculations are evaluated before the data even reaches Tableau
questions.explain: Calculated fields run against the raw data source before aggregation. Table calculations run afterward, recomputing values from what's already been aggregated into the current view.
